In response, the Applicant has submitted one randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study (14CL314) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ENTEREG (alvimopan) 12 mg in the management of postoperative ileus (POI).

This study was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an earlier time period for the preoperative dose: 30 to 90 minutes before the scheduled start of surgery rather than at least than 2 hours before the scheduled start of surgery, as used in four earlier Phase 3 efficacy studies.

design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study (55 US centers), 1:1 randomization to alvimopan 12 mg bid or placebo

citations.quote: In response, the Applicant has submitted one randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study (14CL314) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ENTEREG (alvimopan) 12 mg in the management of postoperative ileus (POI).

Randomization was stratified by sex with subjects being randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive alvimopan 12 mg (as two 6 mg alvimopan capsules) or identical placebo by mouth, given 30 to 90 minutes before the scheduled start of surgery and then twice daily until hospital discharge or for a maximum of 7 days of postoperative treatment.

target_moa.text: Alvimopan is a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor (PAM-OR) antagonist; a selective antagonist of the human mu-opioid receptor (Ki 0.4 nM) that antagonizes the peripheral effects of opioids on GI motility and secretion without reversing central analgesic effects

citations.quote: ENTEREG Capsules contain alvimopan, a peripherally-acting \mu-opioid receptor (PAM-OR) antagonist.
Alvimopan is a selective antagonist of the cloned human \mu-opioid receptor with a K_{i} of 0.4 nM (0.2 ng/mL) and no measurable opioid-agonist effects in standard pharmacologic assays.
Alvimopan achieves this selective gastrointestinal opioid antagonism without reversing the central analgesic effects of mu-opioid agonists.

ENTEREG Capsules contain alvimopan, a peripherally-acting \mu-opioid receptor (PAM-OR) antagonist. Chemically, alvimopan is the single stereoisomer [[2(S)-[[4(R)-(3-hydroxyphenyl)-3(R),4-dimethyl-1-piperidinyl]methyl]-1-oxo-3-phenylpropyl]amino]acetic acid dihydrate.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3% and >=1% placebo) in bowel resection patients were anemia (5.2% vs 4.2% placebo), dyspepsia (7.0% vs 4.6%), hypokalemia (9.5% vs 8.5%), back pain (3.3% vs 1.7%), and urinary retention (3.2% vs 2.1%). Most serious safety signal: a higher number of myocardial infarctions reported with alvimopan 0.5 mg twice daily vs placebo in a 12-month chronic-pain study.

detail.text: A REMS is required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of myocardial infarction; it consists of a communication plan, elements to assure safe use (the E.A.S.E. program restricting use to registered hospitals), an implementation system, a timetable for assessments, and assessments of the REMS.

vote.text: FDA's Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee met January 23, 2008; the committee recommended approval by a 9 to 6 vote with a tighter risk management plan

citations.quote: A meeting of FDA's Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee was held on January 23, 2008 to discuss the safety and effectiveness of Entereg.

The committee recommended approval (9 to 6 vote) with tighter risk management plan to prevent off-label use (>15 total doses), restricting use to in-hospital patients treated by surgeons performing bowel resections only, and the capture of clinical outcomes.
